Tosh, J.

It was originally decided that 10 juniors should represent the Bels., so as not to call upon juniors to race twice, but owing to the absence of Hayman and Ford, through illness, Scrimshaw and Tosh were called upon to compete in two events.

On the same evening we were paid a very high compliment by Surrey A.C., who sent their strongest relay team (Griffiths, Higgins, Wigzell and Dacombe) to wrest from us the "Winstone" Trophy which we won last year at Hook. We were represented by Tosh, J.

Our team for the 4 at 100yds. had an unfamiliar appearance, it being composed of Lander, Tosh, Scrimshaw and Duffett! To our surprise they managed to beat Epsom, Mitcham winning the event from Croydon in 43secs.

Our half-mile cracks, Scrimshaw and Tosh, both found the conditions a little too much for them, while Jack Williams, one of our most promising sprinters, found his dinner troubling him and promptly relieved himself of it!
The fastest time was accomplished by Jim Tosh, who beat Tommy Hampson, the International half-miler and Oxford Blue, in 12 secs. Tosh repeated his time later in the final, beating J.

Jim Tosh seemed determined to win and after the first few yards until within five yards of the tape he was leading. Here Tom Hampson came up with a burst of speed and won by a yard with Tom Scrimshaw slowing down, third.
Tosh (880 yards), J.

The quarter gave Jim Tosh an opportunity to stretch his legs and he returned 52 4-5 secs., being followed home by Beswick, of Ashcombe, and Harold Titherley, who won this event for us one year at Richmond.

A team consisting of Tosh, Scrimshaw, Williams (J.S.), Powter, Gratte, Clemens, Kench, and Ford (A.J.) made up the club team. The start from Baker Street was not at all encouraging, as the rain was descending in torrents, accompanied by plenty of lightning and thunder.

Once again Tosh treated the crowd to some wonderfully fine running in the handicap races. His second in the 880 yards handicap (won in 1 min. 57 secs). off the scratch mark, and win in the 440 yards handicap off 10 yards in 50 secs., speak for themselves.

TOSH, the Hampshire half-mile champion, is his equivalent in handicap races. Tosh (Hampshire, 880 yards), and T. Hampson, the Achilles runner (Surrey, 880 yards), who has also won the Southern title at the same distance.
Webb was leading, very closely followed by Scrimshaw, Tosh and Ford. Soon after, however, Tosh strode into the lead and Scrimshaw went after him, both of them quickly leaving the rest of the field.
Tosh, running in that order. Frank Webb ran a very clever third stage, to gain the lead for us and so gave Jim Tosh a comparatively easy run.

Our team was Titherley, Michael, Jarvis and Tosh, and they were unlucky enough to be drawn on the outside. From the first bend we were behind and remained there until Tosh, running the last "leg," picked up one position and so we finished fifth.
Neither Tosh, the holder, nor Scrimshaw, an ex-champion, started; the former has done hardly any running this year on account of ill-health, and the latter was representing his country.

Scrimshaw did well to win the Scratch half-mile at the British Games, and Jim Tosh to finish second in the Scratch 440 yards. Shields was prominent in the Junior three-quarters of a mile; and our Mile Team and Sprint Relay team also gained awards.
Hampson as a first-claim member and Scrimshaw, Tosh and Cooper Clark all fit and pushing him. Four men beating 1 min. 58 sec. in a club championship?
Tosh, off 1 yard, kept Scrimshaw outside him for the first 100 yards, ran I should think in record time, and then Tommy went up and got on to the heels of Michael, who had taken the lead.
Our team was Michael, Tosh (who took us into the lead), Kench and Scrimshaw; the time of 8 min. 9 secs was good, considering the bad weather conditions.

The five points so earned, with two points gained by Jim Tosh in the 440 yards, were our only scores towards the Trophy, but our representatives generally showed they were worthy to compete in the highest of company which this competition always brings forth.

For us Morgan (100 yards), Tosh (880 yards) and Kench (440 yards) were winners. All the events were keenly contested and we look forward to a renewal of this fixture next year.

Most unfortunately we have been robbed of the best services of two of our usual "star" performers on the track, namely Scrimshaw and Tosh. Tommy seemed to lack sparkle early in the season and eventually the trouble proved to be a growth in the nose which lowered his condition.
